jobs.title: Chief Technology Officer
jobs.description:
At Journal Technologies, we believe our technology can be a force for good in the world ensuring the proper and efficient functioning of some of the most foundational aspects of society - the courts and justice system.

We create and implement enterprise software that supports the administration of justice, currently in the United States, Canada, and Australia. While our eSeries product suite enables governments and their employees to deliver continued foundational court processes, our R&D focuses on leveraging emerging possibilities with technology to improve access and efficiency.

Headquartered in Los Angeles, Journal Technologies is a long-time, wholly-owned subsidiary of Daily Journal Corporation (NASDAQ: DJCO). We also have a major office in Logan, Utah, a team in Melbourne, Australia, an office in Victoria, Canada and a growing number of remote staff across North America.

Under our next generation of leadership, we're implementing a vision for the company that prioritizes building an extraordinary workplace with empowered people at the heart of our business. Great people want to collaborate with great people, and we are actively looking for smart, motivated people who care deeply about the work they do.

Chief Technology Officer

The Chief Technology Officer leads technology strategy, architecture, product development, and engineering across Journal Technologies. This leader sets and champions the technical vision, brings strong product and engineering thinking to every initiative, and ensures the company's platforms remain secure, reliable, and positioned for growth. The CTO works cross-functionally with every department and plays a central role in building out the new technology team described above, helping recruit talent and shape how new ideas are evaluated, developed, and scaled.

What You'll Do

Develop and lead a multi-year technology vision and roadmap aligned with the long-term goals of Journal Technologies and drive it across the organization.
Bring a customer-centric, problem-first approach to product development, ensuring teams deeply understand user needs before committing to solutions.
Identify emerging technologies and market opportunities that strengthen existing products and open new areas of value for the company.
Advise executive leadership on technology investments, build-versus-buy decisions, and potential acquisitions or partnerships.
Define architectural vision and principles, ensuring systems are configurable, repeatable, scalable, secure, appropriately modular, and engineered to upgrade and evolve over time.
Apply platform thinking by promoting reusable services, APIs, and shared components that serve multiple products and business units.
Own the modernization of the Company's technology portfolio, balancing investment in existing platforms with technical debt, modernization, consolidation, and next-generation capabilities.
Lead the engineering organization with a culture grounded in ownership, craftsmanship, continuous improvement, and pragmatic decision-making.
Maintain and advance modern engineering practices, balancing speed of delivery with quality, reliability, and security.
Support our organization-wide transition to Agile methodologies and Scrum-at-Scale.
Serve as a true partner to other departments, building alignment on priorities, timelines, and resources across the organization.
Translate complex technical concepts into clear business terms for non-technical stakeholders, and bring business context back to technical teams.
Build, lead, and develop a high-performing technology organization, including organizational design, leadership development, succession planning, workforce strategy, and recruitment of critical technical capabilities needed for the Company's future.
Ensure appropriate standards for security, privacy, compliance, and data governance, including requirements common to courts, government agencies, and criminal justice systems (such as CJIS).
Oversee technology investment, performance, and operational resilience, ensuring resources are aligned with priorities and systems remain reliable, scalable, and prepared for business continuity.
Establish effective technology governance and risk management, partnering with Security, Cloud Operations, IT, Legal, and business leaders to manage architectural, cybersecurity, regulatory, and third-party technology risks.

Qualifications & Skills

12+ years of software engineering experience, with at least 5 years in senior technical leadership roles (CTO, VP of Engineering, Head of Engineering, or similar).
Proven experience leading and scaling engineering organizations and enterprise software platforms.
Deep expertise in software and systems architecture, including distributed systems, cloud-native design, APIs, and data platforms.
Strong product sense, with experience making customer-driven product decisions.
A track record of setting a compelling technical vision and rallying teams and executives around it.
Proven success working cross-functionally, with excellent communication skills and the ability to engage executives, engineers, customers, and partners alike.
Background in government technology, justice or court systems, legal technology, or other regulated public sector markets is highly desirable.
Experience incubating new products or working in a startup, innovation lab, or venture environment is preferred.
Hands-on experience applying AI, machine learning, and data-driven technologies to real products is preferred.
Experience working within Agile teams or formal training in Scrum or Agile methodologies
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field; advanced degree is a plus.
Given the highly collaborative nature of this role, preference will be shown for candidates able to work on a regular/hybrid basis from our Los Angeles headquarters.

The above statements describe the general nature and level of work being performed in this job function. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties; additional responsibilities may be assigned.

At this time, we are only able to consider candidates who are U.S. (or potentially Canadian) citizens or permanent residents due to employment authorization requirements. We are unable to provide visa sponsorship or work authorization support for this position.

Why Journal Technologies?

Visit Www.journaltech.com/careers For More Information, But Highlights Include

Competitive compensation * The salary range posted for this position reflects a good-faith estimate of the base salary we reasonably expect to offer a successful candidate upon hire. Final compensation will be based on job-related factors, including qualifications, experience, geographic location, and internal compensation considerations.
Quality medical, dental, and vision coverage.
Discretionary profit sharing for eligible employees.
Competitive paid time off as well as paid holiday time.
401(k) retirement (US) and GRRSP (CDN) programs.
Annual professional development funds – minimum $1,500 USD annual per employee (amount depends on role; however, our goal is to invest in our people).
Book subscriptions with an extensive library in each office for personal and professional growth.
Travel opportunities between Journal Technology offices and to interesting client locations.

We provide technology that matters in the world, and we're a stable employer comprised of quality people, with a commitment to investing in our people.

205,000 - 275,000 USD per year(JTI Los Angeles, USA)

200,000 - 270,000 USD per year(United States (Remote))

jobs.title: Senior Director, AI Product Management
jobs.description:
Job Description

Senior Director, AI Product Management

What's the opportunity?

We're looking for a product leader who can turn a strategic product vision into shipped reality at scale. As Senior Director, AI Product Management, you will own user-focused product success for RBC's internal Agentic AI platform, defining the product vision and translating it into a tangible roadmap, community, and ecosystem. You will build discipline around ensuring relentless customer focus and a business-strategy lens on what we build and why. You will lead a team of Product Managers and own Voice of the Customer, feature prioritization, adoption and community building around the product across RBC.

You will be expected to set the operating rhythm, make the hard tradeoff and resourcing calls, and hold a quality bar — bringing the credibility that comes from having built and shipped AI products at scale, not just managed roadmaps.

Your responsibilities will include:

Team leadership: Leading and developing Director-level leads (across Product Strategy & Roadmap, Community & Adoption, Ecosystem & Partnerships) and the teams beneath them, with clear career paths and succession
Integrated delivery: Owning a single execution plan that aligns roadmap delivery, community programs, and partnership milestones to one cadence
Operating cadence: Establishing and running sprint reviews, quarterly planning, and OKR setting and tracking
Tradeoff and escalation ownership: Serving as the primary escalation point for cross-pillar dependencies, tradeoffs, and resourcing decisions
Product quality: Maintaining acceptance criteria, release gates, and documentation standards across the squad
Adoption and outcomes: Using analytics, telemetry, and adoption measurement to drive decisions and report progress, risks, and resource needs
Ecosystem health: Ensuring the community and partnership programs sustain engagement and healthy adoption across the RBC user base

You're our ideal candidate if you:

Have 10+ years of product management experience, including 3+ years leading multi-team product organizations as a manager of managers
Have a track record of customer discovery and translating user needs into product strategy and prioritization
Have hands-on experience delivering end-user facing AI products — ideally generative or agentic AI — at production scale
Have run large-scale internal or enterprise product launches with measurable adoption outcomes
Bring strong operational discipline: agile delivery, OKR frameworks, and release management
Are data-driven, comfortable with analytics, telemetry, and adoption metrics as the basis for product decisions
Have financial services experience, or the ability to rapidly develop it - understanding how banking employees work and the regulatory constraints on internal tooling
Have a working knowledge of LLM evaluation, prompt engineering, or RAG architecture — sufficient to shape product decisions and engage technical teams

Nice to have:

MBA or Master's in a technical or business discipline
Product management certification (CSPO, SAFe, AIPM, or Pragmatic Institute)
Background in platform engineering or developer experience teams
Experience in a major bank's technology or digital transformation function

What's in it for you:

Drive AI transformation at one of Canada's largest and most respected financial institutions, with exposure to senior leadership across RBC
Be part of a newly formed, high-impact function within RBC's AI Group alongside experienced transformation leaders
A comprehensive Total Rewards Program including bonuses and flexible benefits, competitive compensation, commissions, and stock options where applicable
Leaders who support your development through coaching and managing opportunities
Ability to make a difference and lasting impact from a local-to-global scale

About the AI Group:

RBC's AI Group is the AI accelerator for RBC, with a focus on driving the shift from early-stage AI projects to scaled, client outcomes that amplify the impact of RBC's people. In addition to helping scale the biggest AI opportunities at RBC, the AI Group is responsible for advancing research into emerging use cases across generative and agentic AI, while maintaining expertise in security, responsible AI and regulatory expectations.

We are pleased to consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, protected veterans status, Aboriginal/Native American status or any other legally-protected factors. Disability-related accommodations during the application process are available upon request.

jobs.title: Vice President Controlling and Finance PSN
jobs.description:
VICE PRESIDENT CONTROLLING & FINANCE – Parts & Services NASA

Are you a driven leader who sets ambitious targets and thrives on transforming a business? Do you combine strong financial acumen with a close-to-the-business approach? Are you passionate about developing a healthy, high-performing culture focused on operational excellence, continuous improvement, and collaboration?

Our Parts and Service Division in NASA is looking for an experienced Vice President of Controlling and Finance to support business management and deliver focused, accurate reporting that strengthens commercial competence and financial control across the region.

About The Role

As Vice President of Controlling and Finance, you will ensure the delivery of quality-assured and timely financial and non-financial data. This will enable the division to understand its performance against agreed targets, analyze deviations, and proactively implement corrective actions.

In this role, you will be a pivotal member of the divisional management team, participate in business development activities, drive efficiency, and actively contribute to the development of the business in line with our strategy for growth. You will also foster an organization where innovative and efficient people thrive and flourish.

You will be a member of several legal and operational boards within the division’s administrative entities, as well as the Epiroc Financial Council. In this capacity, you will actively contribute to the development of finance and business control practices across the Group.

This is a key position reporting directly to the President of the Parts and Service NASA Division, with a strong connection to the Business Area Controller.

Key Responsibilities

Ensure control over the division’s consolidated financial performance and verify that financial reporting and accounting practices comply with company policies and local regulations.
Gather and present high-quality financial and business data to support strategic decision-making at all levels of the division.
Take ownership of working capital management, proactively reduce overdue payments with the VPs of Marketing and Operations and global functions such as Supply Chain, and establish inventory targets for Customer Centers and regional teams.
Develop a deep understanding of the Parts and Service and supply chain businesses, and advise managers on business cases, investment alternatives, and company valuations.
Lead regional budgeting, forecasting, and financial planning, ensuring alignment between financial targets, business assumptions, and strategic priorities.
Actively challenge and support PSD Global Capabilities on financial planning, return on investment, and capability development.
Continuously monitor and analyze business performance, including active participation in review meetings for Customer Centers, Global Hubs, Supply Chain, and Business Areas.
Identify and interpret business trends, highlight potential risks, and ensure that appropriate action plans are developed and implemented.
Design and deliver tools that provide early warnings of deviations and enable accurate forecasting, helping management avoid unexpected outcomes.
Promote consistent adherence to The Epiroc Way and lead internal and external audit activities, ensuring corrective action is taken when required.
Support strategic acquisitions by coordinating due diligence, developing valuation models, and overseeing financial integration and post-acquisition follow-up.
Provide strong financial leadership and support to the Alternative Offering Business Line, helping establish and develop the new leadership structure, financial governance, and ways of working in alignment with The Epiroc Way.
Build and lead a professional, high-performing finance organization, while strengthening collaboration, team spirit, and financial capabilities across the region.

Experience And Requirements

Strong background as a customer center and product company Business Controller with proven track of delivering results, and of developing a successful, well-motivated organization.
Capability in business process management, and a solid business understanding and interest.
Solid knowledge of financial consolidation/reporting systems.
Experience working in a global organization with multiple factories, distribution centers, and customer markets, including experience from being a manager in a complex international matrix organization and being exposed to corporate risk management.
University degree in finance and/or business administration or similar, relevant field.
Fluency in English is required, both written and verbally. Additional languages are a plus.

Location and travel

Location in an Epiroc office in NASA:

Dallas, US

Belo Horizonte, Brazil

Mexico DF, Mexico

Lima, Peru

Mississauga, Canada

Up to 25% of international travel expected

At Husky TechnologiesTM, our success is based on your success. Our ability to keep our customers in the lead is based on building the strongest team possible.

Husky TechnologiesTM has a strong foundation built on innovation, close customer relationships and a unique culture and values. We are dedicated to offering our customers the highest quality products and services and are looking for people with the inspiration and talent to develop with us as we pursue our ambitious growth strategy. We are a leader in developing state-of-the-art technology and it is this technology base that uniquely positions us to serve customers who seek differentiation through solutions that provide speed, flexibility and maximum productivity. This capability is at the core of our mission and competitive strategy.

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a wealth of opportunity for personal growth and development. Most importantly, Husky Technologies TM offers an opportunity to work with – and be challenged by – a team of great people. Our success is possible because of the creativity, intelligence and passion of our people around the world and their desire to lead change. At the same time, we are not afraid to expect a lot and strive for leadership in all of our key markets. We are a company taking on new challenges and for the right people this means exceptional career development opportunities, the chance to be part of a team that is the best in the world at what we do and the experience that comes from working in an environment that demands constant transformation and innovation.

Husky TechnologiesTM is an exciting company with tremendous potential. We have a great team and great expectations. If you are attracted to bold goals, believe in uncompromising honesty, support mutual respect, care about environmental responsibility, have a passion for excellence and a desire to make a positive contribution – then we want you to join the Husky TechnologiesTM team!

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.
Provide actionable insights and recommendations to improve growth, profitability, and working capital performance.

Business Partnering

Serve as the senior finance partner to service leadership, operations, commercial teams, and Customer Success leaders, providing insight and challenge on strategic priorities, business performance, and investment decisions.
Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.
Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Preferred Experience In a Service Business

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.
Familiarity with pricing strategy, labor productivity, installed base analytics, and customer lifecycle economics

Core Competencies

Strategic leadership
Financial and commercial acumen
Analytical rigor
Executive business partnership
Influence and executive communication
Problem solving
Process improvement
Results orientation and a bias for action

Team Development

Build and lead a high-performing finance team with strong capability in financial analysis, strategic thinking, business partnership, and change leadership.
Lead, coach, and develop team members, including succession planning, capability building, and development of future finance leaders.

Financial Leadership

Provide consistent, timely, accurate, and decision-oriented financial reporting for the service business, with greater automation and self-service access to insights where possible

jobs.title: Site Finance Leader
jobs.description:
Eaton’s Electrical sector is currently seeking a Site Finance Leader to join our CPDI team. This hybrid position is based at our Toronto, ON facility and offers benefits from day one.

The expected annual salary range for this role is $93000 - $117000 a year.

Please note the salary information shown above is a general guideline only. Salaries are based upon candidate skills, experience, and qualifications, as well as market and business considerations.

What You’ll Do

The Site Finance Manager provides direct financial leadership for the Critical Power and Digital Infrastructure business unit, serving as a strategic business partner and change agent to drive continuous improvement and achieve overall business objectives.

This role partners closely with Operations, Sales, Service, and Supply Chain teams to provide financial guidance and actionable insights, drive accountability, and help ensure business strategies and decisions deliver the expected financial and operational results.

Key Responsibilities Include

Analyze financial data and operational performance metrics to identify trends, opportunities, and areas for improvement. Partner with operational leaders to establish key performance indicators (KPIs) and drive accountability for results.
Provide financial insights and analysis to support business decision-making, including capital investment opportunities and resource prioritization.
Drive productivity and profitability through operational excellence, effective supply chain management, and disciplined budget management across the region.
Build organizational capability across both sites by supporting talent development, organizational design, and succession planning.
Partner with Operations to develop action plans, strategies, and initiatives based on financial insights. Monitor execution and measure results through appropriate KPIs.
Develop financial models and scenario analyses to assess potential impacts on operational and financial performance.
Identify financial and operational risks and recommend appropriate mitigation strategies.
Monitor and manage operational costs to improve efficiency and reduce costs while maintaining quality and business performance.
Lead inventory control actions and initiatives to improve operational profitability and optimize cash flow.
Coordinate profit planning and forecasting activities, including analysis of key operational metrics and manufacturing costs.
Lead the planning and deployment of capital investments to support short-, medium-, and long-term business needs. Ensure capital is appropriately prioritized and allocated based on business requirements and cash flow.
Guide sites through Finance Transformation initiatives, including leading change management efforts and implementing best practices that strengthen financial and operational performance.

Qualifications

Basic Required Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field.
Minimum of 5 years of progressive accounting, finance, or controllership experience.
Minimum of 3 years of experience in an operations or manufacturing environment.
Must be legally authorized to work in Canada without company sponsorship now or in the future.
No relocation is offered.

Preferred Qualifications

CPA designation or actively pursuing a CPA designation. CFA or other relevant professional financial designation is considered an asset.
Strong knowledge of Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) and Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) requirements.
Demonstrated experience with financial and data analytics, including translating complex financial information into actionable business insights.
Knowledge of Canadian federal and provincial tax laws and regulations.
Understanding of foreign currency transactions, translation, and financial reporting requirements.
Experience with Oracle Financials or similar ERP systems, including financial system integration.
Strong knowledge of internal controls, financial governance, and risk management.
Experience supporting financial planning, forecasting, budgeting, and manufacturing cost analysis.
Experience partnering with Operations, Supply Chain, Sales, or other cross-functional teams in a manufacturing environment.

What Makes You Successful

You’re a collaborative and proactive finance professional who enjoys turning data into meaningful business insights. You communicate financial concepts in a clear and practical way, build trusted relationships across teams, and are comfortable working in a fast-paced, matrixed environment. You bring strong analytical and Excel skills, manage priorities effectively, and enjoy staying connected to the business by partnering closely with manufacturing teams, including spending time on the shop floor and occasionally visiting other sites.

jobs.title: Director, Technology Operations
jobs.description:
Director, Technical Operations (Platform)

Job Type:
Permanent Full Time

Location:
Hybrid - Toronto, Ontario

Reporting to:
Chief Technology Officer

Salary
: $160,000 – $190,000 CAD

Job Purpose

The Director, Technology Operations owns the operational health of the platforms Goway sells and services travel on: our reservations platform, the infrastructure it runs on, the supplier, air and distribution integrations it depends on, and the automation and data pipelines built around it.

This is a practice-building role. You will define and own Goway's technical operations discipline: service levels, incident management, change control, observability and operational readiness, and you will make them the standard across our technology organisation. You will work alongside other Technology leaders. You will own the technology operations of our platform. You will have the CTO's mandate and backing to build the practice.

What will be your key responsibilities?

Reliability and service management

Define, publish and report service levels and service-level objectives for revenue-critical services, starting with quoting, booking, payment and traveller servicing.
Own incident management end to end: severity definitions, escalation, incident command, communication during an incident, and post-incident review with corrective actions.
Own RCA and problem management.
Own change and release management as a company standard, balancing delivery throughput against change failure rate.
Build observability sufficient to detect degradation.
Own disaster recovery and business continuity for platform services, tested and documented on a stated cadence.

Integration and supplier platform operations

Monitoring of integration paths, error and failure-rate thresholds, and defined fallback behaviour when a partner degrades.
Maintain a dependency map of the external platforms our revenue-generating flows rely on, with assessed operational risk and mitigation for each.
Own operational readiness for new integrations and new product lines entering the platform.
Own the operational reliability of automation and data pipelines in production.

Platform and cloud operations

Day-to-day operation of the AWS and managed hosting infrastructure serving our platform estate: environments, provisioning, patching and lifecycle management.
Own hosting cost governance: visibility by service, a unit-cost measure, and an annual optimisation target.
Lead capacity planning against forecast booking and travel volumes.
Reduce manual, repeatable operational work through automation.
Address seasonal capacity planning, change freezes and enhanced coverage aligned to our booking and departure peaks and to new product launches.

Vendors, partners and compliance

Platform, hosting and integration partner relationships: SLA definition, enforcement and structured performance review.
Reduce single points of dependency, whether on a vendor or an individual.
Partner with security on vulnerability management, patch compliance, access control and audit readiness.

Practice leadership and stakeholder engagement

Build and maintain a multi-year technical operations roadmap aligned to Goway's growth plans.
Report operational performance, risk and investment needs to the CTO and executive team in business terms.

What are we looking for?

Required

8 or more years in platform operations, technical operations, infrastructure or site reliability engineering, including 5 or more years in a lead or leadership capacity.
Demonstrated accountability for the availability and performance of a revenue-critical transactional platform.
Evidence of having built operational practice where little existed: SLOs, incident management, change control and observability introduced from the ground up, with measurable improvement to show for it.
Hands-on depth in AWS, including cost management and multi-environment operation.
Substantial experience operating and governing third-party platforms and integrations, including holding vendors to service levels.
Ability to set standards and drive adoption across teams.
Ability to communicate operational risk and performance.

Preferred

Experience stabilising and operationalising new systems.
Infrastructure-as-code and container orchestration experience.
AWS Certified DevOps Engineer (Professional), or AWS Certified CloudOps Engineer (Associate). Solutions Architect certifications are welcome, but less relevant to this role than the operations-focused ones.
Bachelor's degree in computer science, information technology, engineering or equivalent practical experience.

What can you expect from Goway?

Imagine working for a company where your career feels like an adventure. At Goway, you’ll join a global community that supports one another:
We offer a competitive salary accompanied by performance incentives, and we place real importance on time away from work, such as paid personal days for when life calls for them and your birthday off each year.
Our commitment to professional growth means you’ll have access to continuous learning and industry-leading training that keeps you at the forefront of travel innovation.
You’ll enjoy generous paid time off, including [three] weeks of vacation, [six] personal days, and a dedicated day off to celebrate your birthday.
Travel is in our DNA, so you’ll enjoy exclusive perks and discounts on worldwide getaways.
Since we operate across Toronto, Vancouver, Los Angeles, Manila, Sydney, and beyond, you’ll collaborate across cultures and shape a career path that reflects your ambitions.
Goway is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate differences and are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace for everyone. We appreciate every applicant’s interest. Please be advised that only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

How To Apply

If this role feels like your next step, click "Apply Now" to create your profile, upload your CV, and share a few details about yourself. Our talent team reviews every application, and if your experience aligns with our needs, we will reach out to set up the next step.

AI Screening Disclosure

To help us fairly and efficiently review applications, we use an automated screening process to assess responses to pre-determined questions. This initial step ensures all candidates are evaluated consistently. Qualified applicants will be reviewed by our recruitment team for further consideration.

Additional Notes

Goway Travel Ltd will retain applications, notifications, and records related to this posting for three years, reflecting our commitment to fair and equitable hiring practices.

Recruitment Scams & Fraud Warning

Please be aware of any suspicious emails or WhatsApp activity from individuals pretending to be recruiters or senior personnel at Goway Travel. We will never ask you to install an app during the recruitment process. If you receive a message of this nature, please ignore it and report it to Goway.

About Goway

Founded in Toronto in 1970 by Australian economist Bruce Hodge, Goway has evolved from a one-person dream into a family-owned global leader in tailor-made travel. With our headquarters in Toronto and hubs in Vancouver, Los Angeles, Sydney, and Manila, our team of over 800 talented employees designs travel experiences in more than 115 countries across all seven continents. We’re united by a passion for travel and are committed to doing the right thing: supporting diversity, equity, inclusion, and sustainable tourism that enriches local communities. Whether working remotely or side by side in one of our offices, we operate as one forward-thinking team, transforming wanderlust into life-changing adventures for our fellow Globetrotters. Discover more at goway.com.

Job Description

Senior Director, AI Product Management

What's the opportunity?

We're looking for a product leader who can turn a strategic product vision into shipped reality at scale. As Senior Director, AI Product Management, you will own user-focused product success for RBC's internal Agentic AI platform, defining the product vision and translating it into a tangible roadmap, community, and ecosystem. You will build discipline around ensuring relentless customer focus and a business-strategy lens on what we build and why. You will lead a team of Product Managers and own Voice of the Customer, feature prioritization, adoption and community building around the product across RBC.

You will be expected to set the operating rhythm, make the hard tradeoff and resourcing calls, and hold a quality bar — bringing the credibility that comes from having built and shipped AI products at scale, not just managed roadmaps.

Your responsibilities will include:

Team leadership: Leading and developing Director-level leads (across Product Strategy & Roadmap, Community & Adoption, Ecosystem & Partnerships) and the teams beneath them, with clear career paths and succession
Integrated delivery: Owning a single execution plan that aligns roadmap delivery, community programs, and partnership milestones to one cadence
Operating cadence: Establishing and running sprint reviews, quarterly planning, and OKR setting and tracking
Tradeoff and escalation ownership: Serving as the primary escalation point for cross-pillar dependencies, tradeoffs, and resourcing decisions
Product quality: Maintaining acceptance criteria, release gates, and documentation standards across the squad
Adoption and outcomes: Using analytics, telemetry, and adoption measurement to drive decisions and report progress, risks, and resource needs
Ecosystem health: Ensuring the community and partnership programs sustain engagement and healthy adoption across the RBC user base

You're our ideal candidate if you:

Have 10+ years of product management experience, including 3+ years leading multi-team product organizations as a manager of managers
Have a track record of customer discovery and translating user needs into product strategy and prioritization
Have hands-on experience delivering end-user facing AI products — ideally generative or agentic AI — at production scale
Have run large-scale internal or enterprise product launches with measurable adoption outcomes
Bring strong operational discipline: agile delivery, OKR frameworks, and release management
Are data-driven, comfortable with analytics, telemetry, and adoption metrics as the basis for product decisions
Have financial services experience, or the ability to rapidly develop it - understanding how banking employees work and the regulatory constraints on internal tooling
Have a working knowledge of LLM evaluation, prompt engineering, or RAG architecture — sufficient to shape product decisions and engage technical teams

Nice to have:

MBA or Master's in a technical or business discipline
Product management certification (CSPO, SAFe, AIPM, or Pragmatic Institute)
Background in platform engineering or developer experience teams
Experience in a major bank's technology or digital transformation function

What's in it for you:

Drive AI transformation at one of Canada's largest and most respected financial institutions, with exposure to senior leadership across RBC
Be part of a newly formed, high-impact function within RBC's AI Group alongside experienced transformation leaders
A comprehensive Total Rewards Program including bonuses and flexible benefits, competitive compensation, commissions, and stock options where applicable
Leaders who support your development through coaching and managing opportunities
Ability to make a difference and lasting impact from a local-to-global scale

About the AI Group:

RBC's AI Group is the AI accelerator for RBC, with a focus on driving the shift from early-stage AI projects to scaled, client outcomes that amplify the impact of RBC's people. In addition to helping scale the biggest AI opportunities at RBC, the AI Group is responsible for advancing research into emerging use cases across generative and agentic AI, while maintaining expertise in security, responsible AI and regulatory expectations.

We are pleased to consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, protected veterans status, Aboriginal/Native American status or any other legally-protected factors. Disability-related accommodations during the application process are available upon request.
